### Slide: What ADS-B does NOT tell us

Hook into Part 2:

- **No communications** — what did ATC tell the crew? What did the crew acknowledge?
- **No route intent** — where is the aircraft going beyond the next waypoint?
  (typecode 29 = Target State & Status exists, rarely populated)
- **No contract** — ADS-B broadcasts to everyone, confirmed by no-one;
  no acknowledgement, no negotiation of what to report
- **No oceanic/polar coverage** from ground receivers alone
- **Mode S Comm-B** enriches position with BDS 0x40/0x50/0x60 — but only near a radar

→ Aircraft communicate constantly. All of that goes through **datalink**.


### 2.1 — Communication in aviation (~2 slides)

#### Slide: The "C" in CNS — datalink alongside voice

- Voice VHF (118–137 MHz): primary, ATC instructions near airports
- Voice HF: oceanic, unreliable, progressively replaced
- **Datalink**: digital text/binary messages — alongside or replacing voice
  - ATC clearances (CPDLC), surveillance contracts (ADS-C), airline ops (AOC)
- ACARS operational **since 1978** — predates Mode S by 5 years, ADS-B by 24 years

Contrast with Mode S:
- Mode S DF 20/21: ground *pulls* data near radar sites, BDS chosen by interrogator
- Datalink: bidirectional, global (via satellite), structured application protocols,
  independent of ATC radar infrastructure

#### Slide: The full protocol stack

Each bearer has its own link-layer framing. The ACARS message is a shared
application container that rides on top of any of them.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          APPLICATIONS                                  │
│        ADS-C · CPDLC · ATIS · OOOI · AOC · weather · MIAM             │
└───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                │
         ARINC 622 envelope  ───┴───  ATN B1 (X.25/COTP/ULCS)
         (label H1, /ATSU.IMI.REG)         (VDL2 only)
                                │
┌───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         ACARS message                                  │
│          mode · reg · label · block_id · text · CRC                    │
│       shared format across ALL bearers                                 │
└──┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┬────────┘
   │                      │                  │                  │
 Classic VHF           VDL Mode 2           HFDL            SATCOM
 (MSK, 131 MHz)     (D8PSK, 136 MHz)    (PSK, HF bands)  (L-band/Iridium)
 preamble+sync        AVLC frame           HFDL frame      AMSS/AERO frame
 no link layer    DST·SRC·LCF·FCS      own link layer    own link layer
                  ├─ I-frame (ACARS)    [dumphfdl ref]    [JAERO ref]
                  ├─ I-frame (X.25 → ATN B1)
                  ├─ S-frame (flow ctrl)
                  └─ U-frame (XID)
```

Only the two leftmost bearers are implemented in the `datalink` workspace.
HFDL and SATCOM are documented as architectural context; their ACARS/ADS-C/CPDLC
payloads would reuse the same application decoders once a frontend is added.
